questions.question: Comprehension : The United Nations Secretary-General, António Guterres, this week reiterated the consequences of the climate catastrophe that has enveloped the globe. The earth had passed from a warming phase into an “era of global boiling”, he said at the U.N.’s headquarters in New York. His comments come even as scientific evidence converges on the conclusion that July is set to be the hottest month in the last 12,000 years. This was a “disaster” for the whole planet, he said, noting that “short of a mini-Ice Age over the next few days, July 2023 will shatter records everywhere”. Scientists from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the European Commission’s Copernicus Climate Change Service described conditions this month as “rather remarkable and unprecedented”, with July seeing the hottest three-week period on record. Average July temperature so far has been 16.95° Celsius, 0.2° C warmer than in July 2019 — a record in the 174-year observational data of the European Union. With ocean temperatures on the rise and the Central Equatorial Pacific Ocean transitioning from La Niña conditions — where average sea surface temperatures are below normal — to El Niño conditions, the opposite, it was widely expected that temperatures would be warmer than that in the last three years (when La Niña prevailed). However, it is the distribution and impact of the 16.95° C, which includes temperature in northwest China touching 52° C; wildfires in Greece and the baking heat in the United States’ Southwest. The extraordinarily high rains in north and western India, while largely due to prevailing monsoon conditions, were also due to the warm air increasing atmospheric capacity to hold moisture resulting in short torrential bursts, causing floods and devastation. While climate prognostication induces pessimism, Mr. Guterres said that it was still possible to limit global temperature rise to 1.5° C and avoid the very worst of climate change but only with “dramatic, immediate climate action”. At a G-20 ministerial meet in Chennai the same day, the COP28 President-designate, Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber, also emphasised that the world’s largest economies should be more ambitious with emission cuts. While Prime Minister Narendra Modi has promised to make India the “third largest economy” if his party is re-elected in the general election, it will also mean greater pressure on India to take on a greater share of greenhouse gas mitigation responsibilities. This could mean advancing its net zero commitments from 2070 to 2050, as Mr. Guterres says, and generating fossil-free electricity by 2040. While these are the testy points on which climate negotiations hinge, the climate — it bears reminding — waits for nobody. Q34. Which of the following would weaken the author's argument?

questions.question: Comprehension: Read the following passage and answer the questions given after it . James Herriot, a veterinary surgeon, becomes deeply concerned about a dog named Tricki owned by Mrs. Pumphrey. On seeing Tricki on the street with his owner, he is taken aback by the dog's obesity. His condition reflects a life of overindulgence. Mrs. Pumphrey, a doting owner, admits to pampering Tricki with extra treats like cream cakes and chocolates out of concern for his listlessness. She believes that Tricki might be malnourished, so she supplements his diet with malt, cod-liver oil, and Horlicks. Moreover, the dog's exercise has been minimal since the gardener, responsible for Tricki's play sessions, has been ill.Herriot sternly advises Mrs. Pumphrey to reduce Tricki's food intake and increase his exercise, warning that the dog’s health is in genuine peril. Despite her initial determination, it's not long before Mrs. Pumphrey calls Herriot, distressed. Tricki is now refusing all food, vomiting, and lying around panting.Having anticipated this, Herriot recommends that Tricki be hospitalized for observation. Mrs. Pumphrey is initially resistant, fearing that Tricki would be distressed away from her. Nevertheless, she acquiesces, and Tricki is taken to the surgery, accompanied by a surplus of his belongings, including beds, toys, and coats, most of which are unnecessary.At the surgery, Tricki is initially indifferent to the other dogs. He is placed in a warm box and, for the first couple of days, is given only water. By the third day, Tricki starts showing interest in the other dogs. He begins to engage with them, running and playing vigorously. Through this natural dog-to-dog interaction, Tricki sheds his excess weight and rejuvenates. The once lethargic and sickly pet becomes an energetic, muscular, and happy dog.Throughout Tricki's stay, Mrs. Pumphrey is anxious about his well-being, frequently calling to check on him. To aid in Tricki's "convalescence," she sends fresh eggs, wine, and even brandy. This unexpected bounty becomes a delightful treat for Herriot and his partners, turning their meals into feasts. The vet recognizes the situation's perks, but after two weeks, knowing that Mrs. Pumphrey misses Tricki dearly, he decides it's time for the dog to return home.Upon Tricki's retrieval, Mrs. Pumphrey is overjoyed. She finds it hard to believe the transformation, from an ailing obese dog to a vibrant and healthy one, attributing the change to a "triumph of surgery." As she departs with her rejuvenated pet and the untouched excess of his belongings, Herriot smiles, realizing that sometimes, the simplest solutions, like allowing a dog to be a dog, work wonders.
